sources.title: Venture Capital and the Finance of Innovation
sources.edition: Third edition; April 2021; ISBN 978-1-119-49011-1; publisher catalog states 496 pages
sources.attributionNotes: Supports edition metadata, the four-part architecture, and the publisher's high-level description of high-growth enterprise valuation and preferred-stock valuation. It does not support unpublished formula details.

sources.title: Venture Capital and the Finance of Innovation — Brief Contents
sources.attributionNotes: Supports chapter titles and official chapter starting pages only. No chapter doctrine is inferred solely from a title.

sources.title: Textbook: Venture Capital & the Finance of Innovation
sources.edition: Official third-edition textbook page accessed July 28, 2026
sources.attributionNotes: Supports the book's stated scope: VC finance models, risk and return, historical performance, total valuation, and partial valuation.

sources.title: Venture Capital and the Finance of Innovation — Front Matter and Chapter 1
sources.edition: Third-edition sample; written March 1, 2021; SSRN abstract 929145
sources.attributionNotes: The 36-page third-edition public excerpt was directly reviewed. It contains front matter, the preface, brief contents for Chapters 1-24, and the complete Chapter 1. It supports book architecture, the VC definition, investing/monitoring/exiting scope, and historical stage/industry/region patterns. It does not support substantive methods in Chapters 3-4 or 7-24.

sources.title: The Best Venture Capitalists
sources.edition: Third-edition Chapter 5; written March 1, 2021; revised July 20, 2021; 16 pages
sources.attributionNotes: Supports that the top-tier list is explicitly subjective and uses historical performance, early unicorn participation, and IPO exit rate as discussion inputs. It is not a universal ranking formula.

sources.title: Venture Capital and the Finance of Innovation — Winter 2019 Syllabus
sources.publisher: University of California, Davis Graduate School of Management
sources.edition: Winter 2019 course using the second edition
sources.attributionNotes: Provides an official coauthor explanation of course objectives: Reality-Check DCF, comparables, staged financing, convertible preferred, option valuation, fund economics, risk/return, and real options. It predates the third edition and is used as corroboration.

sources.title: VCV Tools — Overview
sources.edition: Public companion to the second edition, accessed July 28, 2026
sources.attributionNotes: Supports the total-versus-partial valuation workflow and the connection among the VC Method, Reality-Check DCF, comparable exit valuation, term sheets, and division of value among founders, investors, GP, and LP.

sources.title: AUTO Calculator and Exit Diagram Tool
sources.attributionNotes: Supports required term-sheet inputs, the need for all prior rounds, exit payoff schedules, GP/LP division, LP cost, partial valuation, LP valuation, and implied post-money valuation.

sources.title: FLEX Calculator
sources.attributionNotes: Supports component-based partial and LP valuation using option components. It does not by itself validate model assumptions for a given company.

sources.title: Option Calculators
sources.attributionNotes: Supports the named European, random-expiration, and binary option tools and their displayed inputs. Runtime implementation and model validation remain a deterministic-service responsibility.

sources.title: How Do Venture Capitalists Make Decisions?
sources.edition: NBER Working Paper 22587; September 2016; published in Journal of Financial Economics in 2019
sources.attributionNotes: Qualifies the framework with survey evidence from 885 institutional VCs and documents variation by industry, stage, geography, and success. Practice frequency is not normative proof.

sources.title: The Risk and Return of Venture Capital
sources.edition: NBER Working Paper 8066; January 2001; published in Journal of Financial Economics in 2005
sources.attributionNotes: Supports selection-bias, volatility, arithmetic-versus-geometric return, and financing-round risk qualifications. Its historical sample is not a current target-return table.

sources.title: Has Persistence Persisted in Private Equity? Evidence from Buyout and Venture Capital Funds
sources.edition: NBER Working Paper 28109; November 2020; published in Journal of Corporate Finance in 2023
sources.attributionNotes: Qualifies historical fund-performance evidence by distinguishing ex-post results from information actually available at fundraising. It reports remaining VC persistence, but does not justify copying another fund's hurdle.

sources.title: Do Private Equity Managers Earn Their Fees? Compensation, Ownership, and Cash Flow Performance
sources.edition: NBER Working Paper 17942; March 2012; published in Review of Financial Studies in 2013
sources.attributionNotes: Supports treating fees, carry, ownership, cash flows, and LP net performance as separate auditable inputs; market conditions affect compensation. It does not supply universal fee assumptions.

sources.title: Characteristics, Contracts, and Actions: Evidence from Venture Capitalist Analyses
sources.edition: NBER Working Paper 8764; February 2002; published in Journal of Finance in 2004
sources.attributionNotes: Supports the empirical connection among business, management, deal risks, cash-flow rights, control rights, contingencies, and expected monitoring. Associations are not universal causal rules.

sources.title: Financial Contracting Theory Meets the Real World: An Empirical Analysis of Venture Capital Contracts
sources.edition: NBER Working Paper 7660; April 2000; published in Review of Economic Studies in 2003
sources.attributionNotes: Supports separate, state-contingent allocation of cash-flow, voting, board, liquidation, and control rights and the frequent use of convertible securities.

sources.title: Squaring Venture Capital Valuations with Reality
sources.edition: NBER Working Paper 23895; October 2017; published in Journal of Financial Economics in 2020
sources.attributionNotes: Provides empirical evidence that applying the latest preferred-share price to every share can overstate company and common-share value because contractual protections differ.

sources.title: Venture Capital Contracting: Staged Financing and Syndication of Later-stage Investments
sources.attributionNotes: Qualifies the simple real-option account of staging: staging may improve effort and abandonment flexibility but can create investor hold-up and founder-dilution costs; syndication can alter that trade-off.
